Question B-003-019-006.

Why the correct answer is right: The green safety conductor bonds to the chassis so a hot-to-chassis fault has a low-impedance path that helps operate protective devices.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "To the white wire": Neutral-to-ground bonding belongs at the service equipment as required by electrical code, not inside ordinary station power-supply wiring.
- sourceIndex 2: "To the \"hot\" side of the power switch": Connecting the green safety wire to the hot conductor would energize the chassis path and create a lethal fault.
- sourceIndex 3: "To the fuse": The fuse is in the current-carrying circuit; the safety grounding conductor must be bonded directly to exposed metal chassis.
